scope: Read-only static review of candidate-2 server/tests and installed NumPy path loader; no new full run or operational probe.
guardClass: Python audit hook plus repository known-reader wrappers, not an OS sandbox
observations: Repository conftest installs guarded PyArrow read_table/ParquetFile/dataset, Pandas, Polars, Joblib, builtins.open and Path.read_bytes wrappers before test collection.
Installed NumPy path-based load calls Python builtins.open; direct test NPZ reads use freshly generated tmp_path archives.
Server NPZ inputs pass contained manifest/request and byte authentication, or use a just-written temporary archive.
Cockpit research data loading first resolves exact registry authority and authenticates object bytes; operational SQLite/metadata/byte reads are blocked by the pre-import guard.
All located PyArrow read_metadata uses consume in-memory BufferReader objects, from already guarded byte reads.
Static scan found no direct absolute reader call arguments and no server memory_map/OSFile/open_input_file/NumPy memmap/fromfile use.
limitations: The Python audit hook alone cannot intercept arbitrary native extension system calls.
Known-reader wrappers and static call-site review do not establish exhaustive dynamic dataflow or OS-level filesystem/network telemetry.
Zero-access counters in raw guard receipts are policy/covered-boundary assertions, not independent native syscall measurement.
No reachable direct native operational read was identified in this bounded review; full candidate retained identical instrumentation and isolated environment.
